case.case_title: Nanayakkara v. Henry Perera, A.S.P. and Three Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. Application No. 19/85, decided on 9 August 1985

clause.text: Punishment can only be imposed by a competent court and detention before trial is not punishment.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the detention of Vasudeva Nanayakkara was a punishment in violation of Article 13(4) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that his detention was mala fide and constituted punishment, infringing Article 13(4).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued that the detention was lawful, bona fide, for purposes of investigation, and not punishment.
key_facts: The petitioner was detained pending investigation for distributing leaflets and inciting students.
The petitioner admitted distributing leaflets and inciting students.
The detention was authorized under Emergency Regulations for up to 90 days pending investigation.
The Magistrate can investigate if detention amounts to punishment.
The petitioner was released after approximately one month.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court interpreted Article 13(4) as permitting detention pending investigation or trial, provided it is bona fide and not punishment. Detention as punishment without trial is prohibited.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The petitioner admitted the acts leading to detention. The detention was for further investigation and not punitive. The Court found no mala fide or punishment in the detention, thus no violation of Article 13(4).
principles_established: Detention pending investigation is not punishment if bona fide.
Detention as punishment without trial violates Article 13(4).
Magistrates have a role to ensure detention is not punitive.
precedents_cited: Lallubhai Jegibhai v. Union of India A.I.R. 1981 S.C. 728

outcome.holding: The Court held that the detention was lawful, bona fide, and not punishment, thus no infringement of Article 13(4).

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(4) was central to determining whether the detention was lawful or an unlawful punishment; the Court found the detention lawful and not punitive.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner admitted distributing leaflets and inciting students; the detention was for investigation and not punishment, thus lawful under Article 13(4).
